  - paragraph: "Objective: To copy a given line segment using compass and straightedge and verify that the copied segment is equal to the original."

  - article:

    - img "Compass copying line segment to ray CD":
      - slider "Copied endpoint D"
      - text: C D
    - text: Step 1
    - paragraph: With center A, draw an arc of any radius.
    - img
    - text: Step 2
    - paragraph: With the same radius and center C, draw an arc cutting the ray at D.
    - img
    - text: Step 3
    - paragraph: Join C to D.
    - img

    - strong: 0.00 cm
    - complementary:

      - text: Verified! AB = CD
  - paragraph: "ⓘ How to use: Set compass to the length of AB, then from C mark off the same length on the ray."
  - text: Compass radius
  - button "Decrease compass radius": −
  - spinbutton "Compass radius": "5"
  - button "Increase compass radius": ＋
  - button "⌁ Check"
  - article:
    - heading "Worked Example" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Copy AB to ray CD.
    - img
    - paragraph: Here, AB = 5.00 cm and CD = 5.00 cm. Therefore, AB = CD.
  - article:
    - heading "Key Rule / Definition" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Copying a line segment means constructing a segment equal in length to the given segment at a new position using only compass and straightedge.
    - heading "Definition" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Two line segments are equal if they have the same length.
    - img
    - paragraph: If AB = CD, then the segments are equal.
  - article:
    - heading "⚠ Common Misconception" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Changing the compass width while constructing.
    - img: ✕ ✓
    - paragraph: Always keep the same compass width used on the given segment while marking on the ray.
